bibliographic.title: Helical Magnetic Nature of β -Mn Structured CoZn Thin-Films Determined by a Bayesian Approach to Modeling Polarized Neutron Reflectivity Data

affiliations.text: School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Leeds, Leeds LS2 9JT, United Kingdom
ISIS Neutron and Muon Source, STFC Rutherford Appleton Laboratory, Didcot, Oxon. OX11 0QX, United Kingdom
Department of Physics, School of Science, Loughborough University, Loughborough LE11 3TU, United Kingdom

bibliographic.abstract: Chiral magnetic materials can host skyrmions and hence are of interest for numerous spintronic applications including low-power storage. To reach this goal, room temperature operation and a thin film form are needed. We have studied the chiral magnetism in a β –Mn structured CoZn sputtered film, with a Curie temperature of ≈ 130 °C, by means of polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR) in order to reveal its magnetic field-temperature phase diagram. In bulk this material has a helimagnetic ground state. Here we use PNR data to show that the helimagnetism survives in a CoZn film only 100 nm thick, roughly half a helical period. Given the subtlety of differentiating the helical state from a uniform state with reduced interfacial magnetism, we have developed and employed a Bayesian approach that uses model selection to analyze our PNR data and to map out the field-temperature phase diagram of our thin film.

samples.sample_description: Amorphous/polycrystalline cobalt-zinc film with a ZnO capping layer on a SiO2/Si substrate.
